summary.overview: The speaker reflects on a 'book full of butterflies,' symbolizing memories or moments that are delicate and fleeting. They describe these moments as 'fragile' and 'beautiful,' suggesting a sense of nostalgia and appreciation. The speaker acknowledges that these memories are 'gone,' yet they remain cherished, as they 'still remember' them vividly.

The speaker expresses frustration and disappointment in a one-sided romantic relationship. They repeatedly tried to give love and affection ('I tried to give that girl my love', 'And I tried to to give that girl my heart') but felt unreciprocated ('she ain't showing me love'). The speaker feels undervalued, noting that love seems conditional ('Only time they love a nigga is when they see doves'). They describe the relationship as unhealthy ('it ain't feeling healthy') and express skepticism about future love ('The only time I feel ill love again is January'). The speaker also acknowledges the partner's dishonesty ('She had told me that she loved me when she didn’t') and lack of commitment ('it's always been commitment'). Despite the pain ('N it hurt the way you hurt me'), the speaker resolves to move on ('You can tell her it's good riddance').

The speaker regrets their love and wishes to forget the memories ('Id rather wish these memories could be abandoned'). The relationship ended with unanswered questions and lingering hurt ('I got questions from the time that still remain unanswered').

The speaker acknowledges their own financial struggles, noting, 'all my money felt like bills to me, love,' and laments the loss of mutual respect, recalling, 'I miss the days you knew my worth.' They also criticize the partner's insincerity, stating, 'You only call to say 'what's up' to see who out there sippin'.' The speaker concludes by emphasizing the need for sincerity, repeating, 'you need a solo session on sincerity.'

The speaker expresses reluctance to engage with someone who has taken their relationship for granted, as evidenced by 'I’m ducking your calls again / Because in my mind I’m not ready to answer'. They criticize the other person for forgetting how they 'altered my mindset' and for now posting insincere messages about 'strengthening and healing' and 'couple goals without knowing the meaning'. summary.overview: The speaker reflects on a past relationship, describing it as both delicate and intense, comparing it to art shaped by heat but emphasizing it is not 'pandora's box'. They recall the pleasure and emotional depth of their connection, stating it 'yields emotional food for the soul'. However, the relationship ended due to unresolved emotions and arguments, leaving the speaker feeling 'homesick' and conflicted about reaching out. They express pain over their former partner moving on with someone new, feeling their heart has 'grown colder than nights in Chicago'. The speaker acknowledges their own mistakes and regrets, admitting they 'played with fire' and questioning the worth of their actions. Despite the breakup, they still hold lingering thoughts and concerns, hoping their former partner understands their perspective. The song concludes with a plea for understanding, urging their ex to 'cry amongst this river 'til you understand me'.

The speaker expresses deep romantic affection and admiration for their partner, describing them as uniquely crafted ('God took his sweet time with you') and idealizing intimate moments ('Kiss you 'til your lips turn blue'). They highlight a desire for closeness and adventure ('Take me on a date inside my planet', 'Take me on a ship 'cross the Atlantic'). However, there are also moments of doubt and conflict ('Yeah, you're the love of my life and, so why are we fighting?'), where the speaker questions their worthiness ('I hate that you're perfect 'Cause then I ain't worth it'). The bridge reflects a deep emotional connection ('your voice is my favourite tune') and a sense of belonging ('you found where you always belonged'). The final verse introduces themes of loss and unresolved love ('What happens when you give them love and they laugh and leave?'), contrasting earlier idealization with painful memories.

The speaker expresses deep betrayal and hurt over a partner's infidelity, framed metaphorically as squandering 'seven minutes in heaven'. They question the partner's choices, asking 'What if God gave you seven minutes in heaven what would you do ?' and criticize their disloyalty: 'But you chose to be unfaithful and touch among other dudes'. The speaker reflects on the emotional toll, noting 'It's sickening to see that all you needed was 7 minutes' to betray trust. They contrast past love 'worth the moon' with the partner's lies, lamenting 'you capitalized on your lies'. The repeated counting of minutes ('1 minute, 2 minute...') underscores the brevity of the betrayal, yet its profound impact.

summary.overview: The speaker reflects on a woman who was perceived as good and beautiful but had a darker side, described as a 'beast within'. She was 'a light with no darkness in sight' and 'innocent lover', yet she had moments 'worthy for a groupie'. The speaker questions why people glorify the good when the worst aspects come to light, stating, 'Why do we glorify the good when all the worst comes undone?'. The speaker admits they 'never wanted to forgive' but felt bad at the time. The song explores the complexities of love, describing it as worse than drugs, hate, and even doves, stating, 'What’s worse than drugs is love' and 'What’s worse than hate is love'. The speaker acknowledges the irony of seeking love despite its pain, noting, 'We would all preach we wanted love, that’s all that matter'. The song concludes with a repetition of the initial description of the woman, emphasizing her duality.

The speaker reflects on the complexities of gender roles and relationships, questioning societal expectations. They ponder the nature of a woman, describing her as 'a girl with personalities' and questioning why 'your momma made a woman worth the world'. The speaker also examines their own role as a man, wondering if they 'meet your requirements' or are 'too selfish for just thinking you might want a man'. They express confusion and frustration, admitting 'I understand I'm foolish, but what made you wanna mock a man'. summary.overview: The speaker reflects on a past relationship, expressing feelings of attachment and survival rather than mutual living. They criticize their partner for not redefining the relationship ('Baby it stings you should take time to give some redefining') and for reaching out only when lonely ('Don't come around and text a nigga when you're lonely'). The speaker decides to disassociate ('And let me disassociate') and seeks isolation ('So maybe isolation is what I was needing'). They describe the relationship as a 'love affair's a challenge' and acknowledge the emotional toll ('You break me up and build me down but should I let it happen'). The speaker wonders if their partner can see the brokenness of the relationship ('You're stuck in wonderland I wonder then if you could see') and expresses a longing for the past ('I love the way how I used to say I will really miss it'). The song ends with a hope to reconnect ('I hope I find you in this moment, please don't cast away').

The speaker reflects on the qualities of a 'woman written by God,' questioning whether her story is told through her eyes rather than her physical appearance ('Is the story told in her eyes?'). They express a desire for a woman whose character aligns with biblical ideals ('I hope she's described in the Bible scripture') and reject superficiality ('Don't need a lady whose story told by her thighs'). The speaker acknowledges past mistakes ('I've been wrapped around by her lies') and prays for guidance ('I pray one and only, my God's configured'). They critique societal pressures and the objectification of women ('It's hard to pick between the good and then the bad / 'Cause the bad gon' paint the picture that they holy') and emphasize the importance of finding a genuine partner ('Go hunker down and find a woman who's been written by God'). The outro shifts to a personal update about their busy schedule and career ('Today was long, but it was productive').

The speaker reflects on their journey from struggle to success, expressing gratitude to their mother for her sacrifices and guidance. The speaker credits their mother's joy and resilience as a source of inspiration ('I use your joy in cadences I write') and expresses deep love and appreciation ('I love you, ma, I'll never turn back'). They also recall moments of frustration ('I had some times where I got mad') but ultimately recognize the value of their upbringing ('I was raised right, you did that').

summary.overview: The speaker reflects on a failed relationship, questioning whether change from the other person would make a difference now ('And what would be the difference if you changed now?'). They acknowledge that the relationship's end was not solely due to physical distance ('It wasn't just the distance that lost us') and express a sense of uniqueness in their love ('That you can't find this love nowhere else'). The speaker feels conflicted, admitting they are 'blinded by your blank stares' but continue to love persistently ('But I keep loving on and on'). They express regret ('Sorry that it ended') and struggle to understand the other person's actions ('Find why you did it, hurry'). The speaker contemplates the difficulty of letting go ('Mighty hard to sacrifice my love for you') and wonders if they could forget the lies ('If I could find a way to forget all your lies'). The repetition of the question about change ('And what would be the difference if you change?') underscores their uncertainty and unresolved feelings.

The speaker reflects on the nature of love, emphasizing acts of kindness and care for others. For example, 'I wish everybody could love like I love' and 'you see someone, maybe need a hand or something / And you give him a hand and help him out'. The speaker defines love as 'Showing that you care about someone other than yourself'.
